stem: What does continuous integration mean?
options: Merging often with an automatic build and test for each change
Releasing to customers each single hour
Writing most the tests after the release is made
Having one developer review the code each month
explanation: Developers merge changes often and each merge is built and tested automatically.

stem: Which of these is a CI/CD service built into GitHub?
options: GitHub Actions
GitHub Pages
GitHub Sponsors
GitHub Gist
explanation: GitHub Actions runs workflows defined in YAML.

stem: What is the difference between continuous delivery and continuous deployment?
options: Delivery needs a manual release step, deployment releases automatically
Deployment needs a manual release step, delivery releases automatically
Delivery runs the tests, deployment skips them to release faster
Delivery builds the code, deployment only runs the tests
explanation: Delivery keeps every change releasable with a manual release step; deployment releases every passing change automatically.

stem: Where should a pipeline keep the credentials for deployment?
options: In the CI system's encrypted secrets store for the business
In a text file that is committed to the repository
In the name of the branch that is built
In the README of the project
explanation: In the CI system's encrypted secret store, injected at run time, never in the repository.

stem: A pipeline takes 40 minutes because it reinstalls dependencies on every run. What helps most?
options: Cache dependencies and run independent jobs in parallel
Remove the test stage from the pipeline
Run the pipeline just once a week
Build on the developer laptop instead
explanation: Cache dependencies between runs and run independent jobs in parallel.

stem: Which AWS service provides object storage?
options: Amazon S3
Amazon EC2
Amazon RDS
Amazon VPC
explanation: Amazon S3 stores objects in buckets.

stem: What is Amazon EC2?
options: Virtual servers that can be resized on demand in a real project
A managed relational database service
A content delivery network for serving web pages quickly
A queue service for sending messages
explanation: EC2 provides resizable virtual servers in the cloud.

stem: A function must run only when a file is uploaded to a bucket, with no server to manage. Which service fits?
options: AWS Lambda triggered by an S3 event
An EC2 instance running all day long
Amazon RDS with a read replica
AWS Direct Connect to the office network
explanation: AWS Lambda runs code in response to events such as S3 uploads.

stem: What is the best practice when granting permissions through IAM?
options: Grant only the permissions a task needs, using roles
Give each developer the full administrator policy by default
Share one access key across the whole team during the project
Use the root account for daily work
explanation: Grant the least privilege needed, use roles rather than long-lived keys.

stem: A web tier must stay available if one data centre fails. What should you do?
options: Run instances in several Availability Zones behind a load balancer
Run one larger instance with automatic restarts in a single zone
Run instances in one Availability Zone behind a load balancer
Take frequent snapshots so the instance can be restored quickly
explanation: Deploy across multiple Availability Zones behind a load balancer.

stem: Which Google Cloud service provides virtual machines?
options: Compute Engine
Cloud Storage
BigQuery
Pub/Sub
explanation: Compute Engine.

stem: In Azure, what is a resource group?
options: A container for related resources that are managed together
A set of users who share one subscription in most teams for the project
A physical data centre in a region
A virtual network that spans the regions
explanation: A logical container for related resources that share a lifecycle.

stem: Which Google Cloud service runs stateless containers and scales to zero?
options: Cloud Run
Compute Engine
Cloud SQL
Cloud DNS
explanation: Cloud Run runs containers serverlessly and can scale to zero.

stem: Which Azure service manages identities and single sign-on for users and apps?
options: Microsoft Entra ID
Azure Monitor
Azure Blob Storage
Azure Front Door
explanation: Microsoft Entra ID (Azure Active Directory).

stem: An application on a cloud VM must call a storage service without storing keys in code. What should you use?
options: A managed identity or service account attached to the VM
A password written in the source code at that stage during the project
A key emailed to the developers in day-to-day work in most cases
A shared account used by most the services in practice in practice
explanation: A managed identity or service account attached to the VM provides credentials automatically.

stem: What is a Docker image?
options: A read-only template used to start containers
A running instance of an application
A virtual machine with its own kernel
A file that stores just the database
explanation: A read-only template that contains the application and its dependencies; containers run from images.

stem: Which command starts a container from the image web in the background?
options: docker run -d web
docker build -d web
docker push web
docker pull -d web
explanation: docker run -d runs the container detached.

stem: A container is deleted and its database files are gone. Which Docker feature keeps data?
options: A volume mounted into the container in a real project
A larger base image for the container
A second container with the same name
An environment variable with the file path from the start
explanation: Volumes persist data outside the container's writable layer.

stem: What is the purpose of Docker Compose?
options: Define and run several containers from one YAML file
Compile source code inside a container
Monitor the memory use of the host machine for the business
Convert a container into a virtual machine in practice
explanation: Compose defines and runs multi-container applications from one YAML file.

stem: Which Dockerfile practice produces smaller and more secure final images?
options: A multi-stage build with a slim runtime image in day-to-day work
Installing the build tools in the final image too
Running the application as the root user
Copying the whole project folder including .git
explanation: Multi-stage builds copy only the built artefacts into a slim runtime image.

stem: What is infrastructure as code?
options: Defining infrastructure in versioned files instead of manual steps
Defining infrastructure in a wiki page instead of manual steps
Running manual setup steps from a recorded shell history
Defining application code in files that also configure servers
explanation: Managing infrastructure through versioned, declarative definition files instead of manual clicks.

stem: Which Terraform command previews the changes before they are made?
options: terraform plan
terraform apply
terraform init
terraform fmt
explanation: terraform plan shows what would be created, changed or destroyed.

stem: What is the purpose of the Terraform state file?
options: It maps the configuration to the real resources
It lists the users who are allowed to run Terraform
It stores the cloud provider's billing data for the project
It holds the logs of each plan that was ever run
explanation: It records the mapping between the configuration and the real resources so Terraform can compute changes.

stem: Ansible playbooks are called idempotent. What does that mean?
options: Running it again changes nothing if the state is already correct
It runs just once and then deletes itself
It should be run from the server it configures in a real project in the long run
It repeats each task until one of them fails in many setups in a real project
explanation: Running a playbook again leaves the system unchanged if it is already in the desired state.

stem: Someone changed a security group by hand and now the real infrastructure differs from the Terraform code. What is this called?
options: Configuration drift
State locking
Resource tainting
Module versioning
explanation: Configuration drift.

stem: What is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes?
options: Pod
Node
Namespace
Deployment
explanation: A pod, which holds one or more containers.

stem: Which command shows the pods in the current namespace?
options: kubectl get pods
kubectl run pods
kubectl apply pods
kubectl describe nodes
explanation: kubectl get pods lists them.

stem: What does a Deployment manage?
options: Replica pods and their rolling updates
The firewall rules that protect the whole cluster
The storage disks of each node in many setups
The DNS records of the domain for the business
explanation: It maintains a desired number of replica pods and handles rolling updates.

stem: Pods get new IP addresses when they restart. Which object gives clients a stable address?
options: Service
ConfigMap
Secret
Job
explanation: A Service provides a stable virtual IP and DNS name in front of a set of pods.

stem: A pod keeps restarting with status CrashLoopBackOff. What is the best first step?
options: Read the logs and events of the pod
Delete the node that runs the pod and wait a while
Increase the number of replicas to ten
Rename the namespace of the pod from the start
explanation: Read the container logs and the pod events (kubectl logs, kubectl describe pod).

stem: Which command lists the files in the current directory with permissions and sizes?
options: ls -l
cd -l
cat -l
pwd -l
explanation: ls -l shows a long listing with permissions, owner and size.

stem: What does chmod 755 script.sh do?
options: Gives the owner full access and others read and execute
Gives each user full access including write
Removes the execute right from each user
Changes the owner of the file to user 755
explanation: It sets rwx for the owner and r-x for group and others, making the script executable by everyone.

stem: Which command shows the processes using the most CPU in real time?
options: top
df
free
uname
explanation: top (or htop) displays live process resource usage.

stem: What does the pipe in grep error app.log | wc -l accomplish?
options: Counts the lines of app.log that contain error
Deletes the lines of app.log that contain error
Writes the word count of app.log into a new file
Lists the files whose names contain error
explanation: It sends the output of grep to wc, which counts the matching lines.

stem: A service must start at boot and restart on failure on a modern distribution. What is the right tool?
options: A systemd unit enabled with systemctl
An entry added to the user's .bashrc file
A cron job that runs each second for the business
A script placed in the Downloads folder
explanation: A systemd unit file with Restart= and systemctl enable.

stem: Which tool is commonly paired with Prometheus to draw dashboards?
options: Grafana
Jenkins
Ansible
Nginx
explanation: Grafana visualises metrics from Prometheus.

stem: Which three signals make up observability?
options: Metrics, logs and traces in most cases
Builds, tests and releases
Users, roles and policies
Disks, memory and network cards
explanation: Metrics, logs and traces.

stem: What does an SLO describe?
options: A target level of reliability for a service
A contract with penalties for the customer if it fails
A backup schedule for the databases in most teams
A list of all of the servers that run the service
explanation: A target level of reliability, such as 99.9% of requests succeeding in a month.

stem: Which alert is better design for an on-call engineer?
options: Alert on user-facing symptoms such as error rate
Alert on each CPU spike above fifty percent as the work grows
Alert on each log line that contains the word warning
Alert once a day with a long summary email
explanation: Alert on symptoms that affect users, such as error rate, not every CPU spike.

stem: A request crosses six microservices and is slow. Which signal helps find the slow hop?
options: Distributed traces
CPU graphs of one server
Disk usage of the log volume
The uptime of the load balancer
explanation: Distributed tracing shows the time spent in each service along the request path.

stem: What does DNS do?
options: Translates domain names into IP addresses from the start
Assigns IP addresses to devices automatically
Encrypts the traffic between two separate networks for the business
Blocks traffic from unknown devices
explanation: DNS translates domain names into IP addresses.

stem: Which port does HTTPS use by default?
explanation: HTTPS uses TCP port 443.

stem: How many usable host addresses does the subnet 192.168.1.0/24 provide?
explanation: A /24 has 256 addresses, minus the network and broadcast addresses: 254.

stem: Which layer of the OSI model does a router operate at?
options: Network layer (3)
Data link layer (2)
Transport layer (4)
Application layer (7)
explanation: Routers forward packets by IP address at the network layer (layer 3).

stem: A server can be pinged by IP address but the website does not open by name. Which is the first thing to check?
options: DNS resolution of the domain name
The speed of the network cable that is used
The subnet mask of the server in most teams
The battery level of the client laptop
explanation: Connectivity works, so check name resolution (DNS records or resolver).

stem: What is a reverse proxy?
options: A server that forwards client requests to back-end servers
A tool that hides the identity of the client from the websites it visits
A database that caches the pages of a site
A firewall that blocks requests from other countries
explanation: A server that receives client requests and forwards them to back-end servers.

stem: Which of these is a widely used web server and reverse proxy?
options: Nginx
Postman
Docker
Redis
explanation: Nginx.

stem: How do you get a free, automatically renewed TLS certificate for a domain?
options: Use Let's Encrypt through an ACME client
Generate a self-signed certificate once and reuse it
Buy a certificate and install it by hand each year
Copy the certificate of another website in the long run
explanation: Let's Encrypt with an ACME client such as certbot or Caddy.

stem: Which Nginx directive forwards requests to an application running on port 3000?
options: proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
root /var/www/3000;
return 301 http://3000;
explanation: proxy_pass sends requests to an upstream.

stem: Static assets should be served quickly worldwide. Which combination is best?
options: A CDN with long cache lifetimes and compression
The application server with caching switched off
A single large server in one country
A database table that stores the files
explanation: Serve them through a CDN with long cache lifetimes and compression.
